summary: Describes BGP autonomous system confederations, a technique for splitting a large autonomous system into smaller sub-systems. BGP normally requires every speaker in an AS to be fully meshed, which scales badly. Confederations reduce that burden. It is a draft standard, a standards-track status.

eli5.summary: A huge company with a thousand departments cannot have everyone talk to everyone. Confederations split it into smaller teams that talk within themselves and then through their leaders.

questions: how to avoid ibgp full mesh
how do confederations avoid ibgp full mesh
subtitle: Split a huge autonomous system into member systems that look like one AS from outside, so internal BGP no longer needs a full mesh.

tldr.problem: BGP requires every speaker inside one autonomous system to be fully meshed, which needs n*(n-1)/2 internal sessions for n speakers and does not scale.
tldr.mechanism: A large AS is divided into Member-ASes. Inside the confederation they use Member-AS Numbers and two new AS_PATH segment types, while outsiders see only one AS Confederation Identifier.
tldr.outcome: Confederations remove the full mesh requirement and help policy control. RFC 5065 obsoletes RFC 3065 and is updated by RFC 9774.

facts.label: Segment overflow
facts.value: More than 255 ASs starts a new segment

today: RFC 5065 is a Draft Standard that obsoletes RFC 3065 and is updated by RFC 9774. It has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: The Full Mesh Problem
sections.content:
Base BGP requires all BGP speakers within a single autonomous system (AS) to be fully meshed. For n speakers that means n*(n-1)/2 unique Internal BGP (IBGP) sessions, which the RFC says clearly does not scale when an AS has many IBGP speakers.

The RFC names other ways to relieve this, such as RFC 2796 and RFC 1863 (made historic by RFC 4223). BGP confederations are presented as another alternative. The RFC also notes they may improve routing policy control.

This document revises and obsoletes RFC 3065, itself a revision of RFC 1965, with editorial changes, terminology clarifications and more explicit specification based on implementation and deployment experience.
sections.eli5: If every kid in a giant school had to hold a phone line to every other kid, there would be wires everywhere. Confederations cut down the number of wires.

sections.title: Confederation Concepts and Trade-offs
sections.content:
The idea is to subdivide a very large AS into smaller domains, for example all speakers in a geographic region. Connections between those domains then follow the simpler model used for inter-domain connections, which significantly reduces the total number of intra-domain BGP connections.

Four terms matter. An AS Confederation is a collection of autonomous systems advertised as a single AS number to speakers outside it. The AS Confederation Identifier is the externally visible AS number. A Member-AS is an AS inside the confederation, and its Member-AS Number is visible only within the confederation.

There is a cost. Subdividing an AS may make AS_PATH based routing policy more complex for everyone, add maintenance work when the internal topology changes, and may adversely affect optimal routing. Since the internal topology usually does not need to be exposed, the confederation is presented to outsiders as one AS.
sections.eli5: Each class has its own room number that only people inside the school know. Visitors only ever hear the school's name.

sections.title: The Two New AS_PATH Segment Types
sections.content:
The AS_PATH attribute is a well-known mandatory attribute made of path segments. Each segment is a triple of path segment type, path segment length and path segment value. In BGP-4 the 1-octet type field has two values: AS_SET (1) and AS_SEQUENCE (2).

This RFC adds two more. AS_CONFED_SEQUENCE (3) is an ordered set of Member-ASes in the local confederation that the UPDATE message has traversed. AS_CONFED_SET (4) is the unordered equivalent.
sections.eli5: The route keeps a travel diary of places it has passed. Two new kinds of diary entry record only the classes inside the school.

sections.title: Operation and AS_PATH Rules
sections.content:
A confederation member MUST use its AS Confederation Identifier with peers outside its confederation, in OPEN messages and in the AS_PATH. It MUST use its Member-AS Number with peers in the same confederation. A speaker that sees its own Confederation Identifier, or its own Member-AS Number in an AS_CONFED segment, treats the path as if it contained its own AS number, which is loop detection.

When propagating a route, the AS_PATH is changed depending on the receiver:

  • Same Member-AS: the AS_PATH is not modified.
  • Another Member-AS of the confederation: the speaker prepends its own Member-AS number to a leading AS_CONFED_SEQUENCE, or creates a new AS_CONFED_SEQUENCE segment if the first segment is not one or the path is empty. If a segment would exceed 255 ASs, it SHOULD start a new segment.
  • Outside the confederation: all AS_CONFED_SEQUENCE and AS_CONFED_SET segments MUST be removed first. Then the speaker prepends its AS Confederation Identifier to a leading AS_SEQUENCE, or creates a new AS_SEQUENCE segment.

For routes a speaker originates, the AS_PATH is empty (length field zero) toward its own Member-AS, holds its Member-AS Number in an AS_CONFED_SEQUENCE toward other Member-ASes, and holds the Confederation Identifier in an AS_SEQUENCE toward outsiders. By local configuration, a speaker MAY prepend more than one instance of its value.
sections.eli5: When a message leaves a class it gets a class sticker. When it leaves the school, all class stickers are peeled off and one school sticker goes on.

sections.title: Error Handling and Path Selection
sections.content:
A speaker MUST NOT send AS_CONFED_SET or AS_CONFED_SEQUENCE segments to peers outside the confederation. Receiving them from such a neighbor is an error, and the message is treated as having a malformed AS_PATH under the UPDATE message error handling of BGP-4. The same applies to an update from a confederation peer in a different Member-AS whose first segment is not an AS_CONFED_SEQUENCE. The RFC says this section applies to all BGP speakers, not only confederation members.

Path selection inside a confederation follows the same rules as inside one AS, plus these:

  • If the AS_PATH has only AS_CONFED segments, the neighbor AS is the local AS.
  • Otherwise, the neighbor AS is the leftmost AS_SEQUENCE AS.
  • AS_CONFED_SEQUENCE and AS_CONFED_SET SHOULD NOT be counted when comparing AS_PATH length.
  • A route from a peer in the same confederation (not necessarily the same Member-AS) is treated as internal.

MEDs of two routes SHOULD only be compared if the first AS in the first AS_SEQUENCE is the same. The restriction on sending LOCAL_PREF to a neighboring AS within the same confederation is removed, and an unchanged NEXT_HOP and MED may be advertised to a neighboring Member-AS.
sections.eli5: The school has rules for when a message looks wrong. A class sticker showing up from outside the school is a sign something is off, so the message is rejected.

sections.title: Compatibility and Deployment
sections.content:
All speakers that are members of a confederation MUST recognize the two new segment types. A speaker without support generates a NOTIFICATION for an UPDATE Message Error with sub-code Malformed AS_PATH. Speakers outside the confederation need not support the extensions.

The RFC states that confederations have been widely deployed for a number of years and are supported by multiple vendors. Bad configuration can duplicate routing information, waste resources, cause route flaps and delay convergence. Confederations, like route reflectors, can also produce permanent oscillation between candidate routes, as shown in RFC 3345. One suggested avoidance is configuring inter-Member-AS IGP metrics higher than intra-Member-AS ones.

Member-ASes may share one IGP or each run their own, in which case NEXT_HOP may need to be set by policy. Aggregation inside a confederation is not generally used; if done, AS_CONFED segments MUST be kept separate from AS_SET and AS_SEQUENCE segments.
sections.eli5: Everyone inside the school must know the new sticker rules. Outsiders do not have to, since they never see the stickers.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The extension does not change the underlying security issues of BGP, such as those described in RFC 2385 and in the BGP vulnerabilities analysis. The RFC adds no new protections of its own.
sections.eli5: Splitting into classes does not make the school any safer or less safe. The old risks stay the same.
